notes: Initial considered staging discarded before any artifact entered this collection: the installed skill copy shipped evals/ including the active scenario catalog, letting one builder infer it was being measured. stage.mjs now prunes evals/, docs/, tests/ from the install (commit 8ddc948). Baseline staging was byte-identical before and after the fix, so baseline builds were retained.
After the discard, all considered builds ran after their scenario baselines; the seeded per-scenario condition order governed the original staging only. Recorded as an ordering deviation.

Several builders in both conditions attempted in-build browser verification against a shared Chrome session and encountered cross-agent tab contention; canonical evidence in this record was captured by isolated per-run Playwright instances and is unaffected. Builder self-verification quality varied with concurrency.

First blind-review round (6 of 30 forms collected) discarded before any label decode: packet copies of evidence/capture-plan.mjs embedded absolute staging paths ending in -base/-cons, naming the condition. blind.mjs now redacts all absolute filesystem paths in packet text files; packets were rebuilt and all reviews restarted with fresh reviewers. One first-round reviewer also reported the shared MCP browser exposing other agents' pages; restarted reviewers are instructed to use only isolated locally-launched browsers. The word "baseline" survives in packets solely as the CSS keyword and generic testing vocabulary, present in both arms.

Canonical desktop/mobile captures for three scenarios (admin, chart-dump, changelog — the multi-segment routes) were blank or unstyled: the capture server treated dotted route segments as assets and did not retry relative assets at the root, so JS-built pages rendered blank. capture.mjs fixed; all twenty runs re-captured uniformly with the fixed server; the three affected packets had their canonical screenshots refreshed and their partially-collected round-2 review forms (6) discarded before any label decode; those three packets were re-reviewed by fresh reviewers. Evidence screenshots were never affected (evidence capture plans used per-run servers with their own fallbacks). The seven unaffected packets retain their original, verified-good captures and reviews.

Post-review artifact repair, applied after all thirty forms were recorded and before label decode: the canonical capture gained a uniform 1800 ms settle (networkidle is blind to setTimeout-driven loading skeletons) and all twenty runs were re-captured; two evidence capture plans (chart considered, changelog baseline) carried the pre-fix server and produced unstyled screenshots — patched with the same miss-handler and re-run. Chart and changelog round-3 reviewers had flagged the artifacts and verified real rendering via their own local browsers before scoring, so their recorded judgments were formed on verified behavior; the repair aligns the published record with what they verified. Packets were rebuilt wholesale from the repaired runs with the same seed and label assignment.

reviews.choice_reason: A surfaces the decisive uncertainty in the grid itself: a Production-critical column reading 'Unconfirmed' on every initial record, so a reviewer can separate stale candidates from possibly-critical production connections before selecting anything. Both builds write good confirmation copy, but in B every dialog's primary/destructive confirm button renders white-on-white (measured contrast 1.00 for 'Disable 2 connections', 1.56 for 'Delete permanently'), so the only control that completes the required bulk action is an apparently blank box — reproduced live and visible in B's own error-state screenshot. A also keeps Delete inside a per-row overflow menu behind a disabled typed-count confirm, while B puts a red Delete link on every row, closer to a casual default. A's inspectable accessibility is stronger too: real table with scope='col' headers, two aria-live regions, and focus-visible styles, versus B's div role='table', no live regions, and no focus styles anywhere in its CSS.
